Dana Announces Pricing, Expiration and Results of Tender Offers for Any and All of its Outstanding 4.250% Senior Notes due 2030 and 4.500% Senior Notes due 2032 4 min read

DAN MAUMEE, Ohio, Nov. 13, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Dana Incorporated ( DAN ) ("Dana" or the "Company") announced today the pricing, expiration and results of its tender offers to purchase for cash any and all of its outstanding 4.250% Senior Notes due 2030 (the "2030 Notes") and 4.500% Senior Notes due 2032 (the "2032 Notes" and, together with the 2030 Notes, the "Notes"). The tender offers (each, an "Offer" and, together, the "Offers") were made pursuant to the Offer to Purchase, dated November 6, 2026 (the "Offer to Purchase"). The Offers expired at 5:00 p.m., New York City time, on November 13, 2026 (the "Expiration Date"). According to information provided by D.F. King & Co., Inc., the tender and information agent for the Offers, $357,873,000 aggregate principal amount of Notes were validly tendered by the Expiration Date and not validly withdrawn by the Withdrawal Deadline (as defined in the Offer to Purchase). The table below includes information about the aggregate principal amount of Notes referred to above broken out between 2030 Notes and 2032 Notes. The table below also shows pricing information regarding the Notes, including the Consideration (as defined below) for the Notes, calculated as of 3:00 p.m., New York City time, today, November 13, 2026, in accordance with the Offer to Purchase. (1) No representation is made as to the correctness or accuracy of the CUSIP numbers or ISINs listed in this news release or printed on the Notes. Such information is provided solely for the convenience of the holders of the Notes (each, a "Holder" and, collectively, the "Holders"). (2) Reflects the consideration (the "Consideration") for each $1,000 principal amount of Notes of each series validly tendered, not validly withdrawn and accepted for purchase pursuant to the Offers. In addition to the Consideration, Holders whose Notes are accepted for purchase pursuant to the Offers will also receive accrued interest ("Accrued Interest") on such Notes from the last interest payment date of such Notes to, but not including, November 17, 2026 (the "Settlement Date"). Interest will cease to accrue on the Settlement Date for all Notes accepted for purchase.

The Company intends to accept for purchase the principal amount of the Notes specified in the table above and pay the applicable Consideration and Accrued Interest for such Notes on the Settlement Date. To the extent any Notes remain outstanding following the consummation of the Offers, the Company currently intends to (but is not obligated to) defease all covenants (except payment of principal and interest and maintenance of office) with respect to one or both series of Notes, in which case Holders of such Notes will continue to receive interest on each scheduled interest payment date and principal on the stated maturity date but will not benefit from any restrictive covenants removed pursuant to the defeasance, including the change of control repurchase obligations. The description of the Offers above is only a summary and is qualified in its entirety by the Offer to Purchase. Information Relating to the Offers The Company retained J.P. Morgan Securities LLC and Barclays Capital Inc. as dealer managers in connection with the Offers (the "Dealer Managers"). In such capacities, they may contact Holders regarding the Offers and may request brokers, dealers, commercial banks, trust companies and other nominees or intermediaries to forward the Offer to Purchase and related materials to beneficial owners of Notes. Requests for documents may be directed to D.F. King & Co., the tender and information agent, at: (866) 796-3441 (toll-free) (bankers and brokers can call collect at (212) 257-2516) or dana@dfking.com . Questions about the Offers may be directed to J.P. Morgan Securities LLC at (866) 834-4466 (toll-free) or (212) 834-3554 (collect) or Barclays Capital Inc. at (800) 438-3242 (toll-free) or by email at us.lm@barclays.com . This news release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell, or a solicitation of an offer to buy, any security. No offer, solicitation or sale has been or will be made in any jurisdiction in which such an offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful. The Offers were only made pursuant to the Offer to Purchase. About Dana Incorporated Dana Incorporated ( DAN ) is a global leader in the design and manufacture of highly efficient propulsion solutions for the light- and commercial vehicle markets. Guided by its vision to be the world's best powertrain company, Dana delivers advanced conventional and clean energy technologies that help customers improve the performance, efficiency, and durability of their vehicles. The company supplies leading vehicle manufacturers and related aftermarkets with industry defining drive systems, electrodynamic technologies, and thermal and sealing solutions. item.content:encoded:
News / GuruFocus / Strategy Stocks Fall 3.64% as Bitcoin Breaks $70,000 Ahead of MSCI Exit

Strategy Stocks Fall 3.64% as Bitcoin Breaks $70,000 Ahead of MSCI Exit 1 min read

MSTR BTCUSD Strategy MSTR shares fell 3.64% to $110.24 as of 10:05 a.m. ET in Friday's regular session on November 13, as Bitcoin slid about 3% to $69,342, its first drop below $70,000 since August. The decline comes days after MSCI confirmed it will remove Strategy from its indexes after the close on November 30. The index decision is the first under MSCI's new rule for companies that look more like investment funds than operating businesses. It removes Strategy from the MSCI USA, World and ACWI indexes, according to 24/7 Wall St. Strategy had estimated that about $2.8 billion of its shares could be sold as a result, and J.P. Morgan put potential outflows at up to $8.8 billion if other index providers follow. Strategy held about 848,517 Bitcoin as of October 25, bought for $64.02 billion, an average of roughly $75,446 each.

At $69,342, Bitcoin sits about 8.1% below that average cost. That matters because Strategy funds purchases by selling shares and debt, and a price below cost makes new capital harder to raise. The GuruFocus chart shows a GF Score of 67/100, with decent momentum but weak profitability and an average balance sheet for a company whose earnings swing with Bitcoin. GF Value is $111.04, almost exactly the share price, with a "Fairly Valued" label, and the shares trade at 0.84 times book value. The model sees no edge either way, which leaves Bitcoin as the deciding variable. The next test is the November 30 index deletion and whether Bitcoin holds above its August lows.

Injective: Voting opens on Veyra Mainnet Upgrade proposal - 12 Nov 2026 Less than 1 min read

INJUSD Injective opens voting on the Veyra Mainnet Upgrade proposal on 12 Nov 2026. The proposal covers infrastructure for institutional use of real-world assets (RWAs), expanded enterprise gateways and groundwork for native privacy through CypherOS. A passing vote would advance the proposed protocol expansion for INJ. Approval would move the proposal through governance, but the upgrade itself would still be pending activation. Voting does not activate the proposed changes.

JUPUSD Jupiter launches Baskets on 12 Nov 2026, giving users a way to own a curated set of tokens through a single deposit. Users can access the new feature on Jupiter's platform. Baskets can route more trading activity through Jupiter as users access curated token sets on the platform. For the JUP token, the potential benefit comes from greater platform usage. The launch does not change the token's economics.
